1  *************
 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as follows:
That on 02.03.2021 at about 2.00 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in TVX XL motorcycle bearing No.KA-42-J-2187 along with his son Anil Kumar B.N., from Bettegowdanadoddi village towards Kanakapura side, on the extreme side of Kanakapura road and when he reached in front of Government School, near Kurupete, Kanakapura-Kodihalli road, Kanakapura town, Ramanagara District, at that time, the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained severe injuries all over his body.

He was immediately shifted to Government Hospital,
kanakapura, and thereafter to General Hospital, Jayanagara, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
A case was registered in Crime No.11/2021 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC against the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-M-0882.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
3. In response to the notice of the petition, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 have appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and have filed their written statement separately.
The first respondent in his written statement has denied the petition averments as false.

The first respondent is the owner/driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882 and he is having valid driving license and valid insurance policy in respect of his car with the second respondent.
The accident took place not due to the negligence on his part, but only due to the negligence of petitioner's son.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
The second respondent-insurance company in its written statement has denied the entire petition averments as false.

RC owner of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882 i.e., first respondent has failed to comply with the the terms and conditions of the policy if at all any policy was issued by the second respondent.
The first respondent and the jurisdictional police have not complied with the mandatory requirements under Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The first respondent was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.

The rider of the TVS XL motorcycle rode the same without having valid DL and without observing any traffic rules and he himself caused accident, due to which the petitioner sustained injuries, but there is no fault of the car driver and as such, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation.
There was six days delay in lodging the complaint regarding the said accident.

The petitioner by colluding with the police Nagaraju vs Kumara on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88905211/
2 have falsely implicated the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882 and filed a false complaint to claim wrongful gain.
The petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant and fanciful.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882 by its driver, dashed to the petitioner who was proceeding as pillion rider in the TVX XL motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-42-J-2187 and he sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 02.03.2021 ?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of rider of motor cycle ?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is he quantum of compensation and from whom?
4.
What order ?
5. On behalf of the petitioner, he got himself examined as PW-1 and one witness was examined as PW-2 and got marked Exhibits P.1 to P.19.
The respondents have not chosen to lead any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
6. Heard the arguments of both sides.

7. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative,
Issue No.2 ... In the negative Issue No.3 ... Partly in affirmative, awarding compensation  of Rs.4,02,000/- from the respondents Issue No.4 ...

As per final order, for the following:-
 REASONS  8. Issue Nos.1 & 2: Since these issues are interconnected, I have taken them together.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, is relying upon his oral evidence and documentary evidence such as FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, seizure panchanamas, spot sketch, IMV report,
wound certificate, chargesheet, notice under Sec.133 of MV Act and reply to the said notice as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.

PW.1 in his affidavit evidence has narrated the manner in which he met with an Nagaraju vs Kumara on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88905211/
3 accident and accident was due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882.
The respondents No.1 and 2 have filed their written statement wherein they have denied the accident and also the negligence aspect.

Second respondent has contended that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the TVS XL motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-42-J-2187 and there was six days delay in lodging the complaint and the insured car has been falsely implicated in this case by the petitioner by colluding with the police.
Let us consider the evidence placed by the parties to decide these issues.

9. As per PW.1, on 02.03.2021 at about 2.00 p.m., when he was travelling as a pillion rider in the TVS XL motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-42-J-2187 from Bettegowdanadoddi Village towards Kanakapura side along with his son Anil Kumar B.N., who was the rider of the said motorcycle and when the said motorcycle reached in front of Government Hospital near Kanakapura-Kodihalli road,
at that time, the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882 has driven it from Kodihalli side towards Kanakapura side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorbike from behind, which resulted in accident.

10. FIR and the complaint as per Exs.P.1 and P.2 disclose that on the basis of the complaint lodged by the son of the petitioner, a criminal case was registered against the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882.
Accident occurred on 02.03.2021, but the complaint was lodged on 06.03.2021.
Thus, there is delay of 4 days in lodging the complaint.
PW.1 in his cross-examination has admitted that after 5 days of occurrence of the accident, complaint was lodged by the complainant.
In the complaint - Ex.P.2, it is mentioned that as there was nobody to look after his father, the complainant after providing treatment to his father, has lodged the complaint.
In view of the complainant explaining the delay in lodging the complaint, I am of the opinion that the reason assigned by the son has to be accepted as genuine reason.
Merely because there was delay of 4-5 days in lodging the complaint, the claim of the petitioner cannot be doubted when the petitioner has given plausible explanation for delay.
11. Exs.P.3 and P.6 are the spot mahazar and the spot sketch which reveals the state of affairs at the accident spot.

As per these documents, the place of accident is opposite to Government Primary School near Kurupete of Kanakapura town, on Kodihalli-Kanakapura main road and the place of accident is about 3 ft. away from the left side edge of the road.
The width of the said road is about 22 ft., and it runs north to south.

Even by considering these documents, it can be said that the rider of the motorcycle was moving on the left side of the road and at that time, the driver of the car has hit the car to the motorcycle from behind, which resulted in accident.
12. Exs.P.4 and P5 are the seizure mahazars under which the police have seized both the vehicles involved in the accident.
In these documents, the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
As per Ex.P.4, the front handle, right side leg guard, right side front foot rest, right side silencer of the motorcycle have been damaged.
In Ex.P.5, it is mentioned that the right side mirror of the car and left side front bumper were damaged and there is scratch marks on right side back door of the car.
Even in Ex.P.7-IMV report, the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.

As per Ex.P.7, head light, crash guard, front right side foot rest of the motorcycle were damaged,
whereas the front right side rear view mirror of the car was damaged.

By considering these damages Nagaraju vs Kumara on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88905211/
4 mentioned in the seizure mahazars and the IMV report, it can be said that the car driver has dashed his car against the TVS XL motorcycle from backside and as such, those damages are caused to the vehicles in accident.
13 Ex.P.8 is the wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner has sustained injuries in accident.
Ex.P.9 is the chargesheet filed by the police against the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882, after detailed investigation.
This chargesheet, was not challenged by the driver of the car.
Even in the chargesheet, it is alleged that the driver of the car by driving it with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, has dashed the motorcycle of the petitioner from back side.

Exs.P.10 and P.11 are the notice issued to the owner of the car and the reply given by the said owner wherein the driver of the car who is none other than the first respondent, has stated that he himself was driving the car and after the accident, due to fear he went away from the spot without stopping the car and the documents of the vehicle were in force at that time.
Even by considering Exs.P.10 and P.11, it can be said that it is the driver of the car i.e., the first respondent who has caused the accident resulting in injuries to the petitioner.
Though the respondents have denied the accident and negligence aspect, but they have not chosen to place any cogent evidence to disprove the evidence placed by the petitioner.
Even the first respondent has not chosen to lead his evidence to controvert the evidence placed by the petitioner.
As such, the contention of the respondents remained unproved.
On the other hand, the evidence placed by the petitioner remained unrebutted.

The conduct of the first respondent in not challenging the chargesheet itself is sufficient to draw an adverse inference against him that as the accident took place due to his negligence, he has remained silent.

14. The learned counsel for the second respondent during his arguments, has submitted that as the rider of the motorcycle was riding it without having valid DL, due to his negligence also accident has occurred and as such, 25% of the contributory negligence has to be fixed on the rider of the motorcycle.
Nowhere in the written statement the second respondent has contended that the rider of the motorcycle has contributed negligence in occurring of the accident.
As discussed above, this court has come to the conclusion that the evidence on record clearly establishes that sole negligence was on the part of the car driver and not the rider of the motorcycle.
Therefore, the arguments of the learned counsel for the second respondent cannot be accepted.

Thus, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved that he met with an accident and sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M- 0882, whereas the first respondent has failed to prove that accident occurred on account of negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-42-J- 2187.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative and Issue No.2 in the negative.

15. ISSUE No.3:
(a). Pain and Agony:
Wound certificate-Ex.P.8 discloses that the petitioner has sustained fresh abrasions over right elbow joint and right knee, swelling over right ankle joint, pain and Nagaraju vs Kumara on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88905211/
5 tenderness over right ankle joint and loss of movement at right ankle joint.
X- ray shows right side calcaneal fracture with Ipsilateral medial malleoli fracture.
As per the opinion of the doctor, the said injuries No.1 and 2 are simple in nature and injuries No.3 to 5 are grievous in nature.
Discharge Summary at Ex.P.15 discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment in General Hospital, Jayanagar as an inpatient from 02.03.2021 to 22.03.2021.
Ex.P.16 is the outpatient record of the said hospital, which discloses that after the discharge, the petitioner has taken follow-up treatment in General hospital, Jayanagar, Bengaluru.
As per these documents, the petitioner has undergone surgery with close reduction and internal fixation.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner requires minimum four months treatment.
During treatment period, the petitioner has suffered lot of pain and agony.

As such, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under the head pain and agony.

(b). Medical Expenses (including conveyance, attendant charges and extra nourishment):
PW-1 has deposed that, he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, nourishment and attendant charges etc.
In support of his evidence, PW.1 has produced only two medical bills at Ex.P.17 for Rs.1,063/-.

One bill is of government Hospital, Jayanagar and another bill is of Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Except these bills, the petitioner has not produced any other bills to prove that he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
As the hospital in which the petitioner has taken treatment is a Government Hospital, the treatment will be free and as such, the petitioner has not produced medical bills except Ex.P.17.

By considering the number of days of treatment in General Hospital, Jayanagar and by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has spent some amount towards medicines, nourishment and attendant charges.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.
(c) Loss of income during the treatment period:

PW-1 has deposed that, prior to the accident he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month by doing agricultural and sericulture works at Bettegowdanadoddi village, but due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of earnings.
In support of his evidence, PW1 has produced the RTCs as per Ex.P.13.
These documents disclose that the joint family of the petitioner is owning lands and the name of the petitioner finds place in some of the RTCs.
By considering that the joint family of the petitioner owns some lands, it can be said that the petitioner was having income from the said lands.
As such, the income of the petitioner from his lands is taken at Rs.15,000/- per month.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner requires four months treatment.
During the treatment period, the petitioner has suffered loss of income.

As such, I Nagaraju vs Kumara on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88905211/
6 deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.60,000/- under the head loss of income during the period of treatment.

sentences.text: (d) Future loss of earning capacity:

PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is getting unbearable pain often, he cannot walk or stand or sit, squat or carry any weight, cannot do any routine work and he cannot expose himself to sun light and he has partial headache and as such, he has suffered permanent disability resulting in loss of earning capacity.

In order to prove the disability, the petitioner has examined the doctor as PW.2 and PW.2 has deposed about the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the line of treatment undergone by the petitioner.
As per PW.2, the petitioner suffers from disability of right lower limb at 28.29% which is 14.1% to the whole body.
Whether the disability assessed by PW.2 is to be accepted or not has to be scrutinized cautiously.

PW.2 in his cross-examination has admitted that he has not given any treatment to the petitioner, but he has examined the petitioner only for the purpose of assessing the physical disability of the petitioner and the alleged stability component regarding the petitioner is only mild in nature.

Merely because PW.2 is not the treated doctor of the petitioner, his evidence cannot be brushed aside when he is a competent person to assess the disability since he is also a senior consultant and DNB of Orthopaedics.
As the petitioner is an agriculturist, it can be said that the disability stated by PW.2 will definitely reduce the earning capacity of the petitioner to some extent.
As per PW.2, the fractures are united.
As such, I am of the opinion that the functional disability is to be taken at 10%.

The income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.15,000/-
per month.
The annual income of the petitioner is Rs.1,80,000/-.
PW.1 has deposed that he was aged about 55 years at the time of accident.
In order to prove the age, PW.1 has produced his Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.14.
In Ex.P.14, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 01.01.1962.
by considering this date of birth, it can be said that the petitioner was aged 59 years as on the date of accident.

Depending upon the said age of the petitioner, as per the ratio laid down in the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation),
the proper multiplier applicable is 9.

PW.1 has deposed that another surgery is required for him in future and its expenses will be more than Rs.1,00,000/-.
PW.2 has deposed that he has advised the petitioner to undergo another operation for removal of implants.
The medical records of the petitioner disclose that he has undergone surgery by fixation of implants.

(f) Towards unhappiness and loss of amenities:
PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is getting unbearable pain often, he cannot walk or stand or sit, squat or carry any weight, cannot do any routine work and he cannot expose himself to sun light and he has partial headache.

PW-2 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has complications like infection, deformity, loss of sensation, there is restriction of movements in the right ankle joint and foot and the petitioner has difficulties to stand, sit, walk, climb, squat,
kneel etc., and he suffers from disability of 28.29% to the right lower limb and 14.1%
to the whole body.
These difficulties stated by PWs1 and 2 will definitely cause unhappiness and discomfort to the petitioner while doing his normal activities and also while doing his avocation.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.70,000/- under this head of unhappiness and loss of amenities.

16. In view of the reasons stated above, in all the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:

c. Loss of income during the Rs. 60,000-00  treatment and rest period  15000x4 d. Loss of future earning capacity Rs. 1,62,000-00  15000x12x10x9/100 e.
Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000-00 d. Unhappiness and loss of Rs. 70,000-00
amenities

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,02,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., excluding Rs.30,000/- awarded under the head future medical expenses, from the date of the petition till deposit in Court.

8 17.
So far as the liability is concerned, according to the petitioner, the first respondent is the owner and the second respondent is the insurer of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-M- 0882.
First respondent in his written statement has contended that he is the owner of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882 and the RC, tax card and insurance policy of the car are in his name.
The second respondent has not admitted the issuance of insurance policy as per the particulars given by the petitioner, for want of confirmation from its issuing office.
However, the petitioner has produced the copy of the policy.

The said policy stands in the name of the third respondent who is dead and he was deleted from the petition on the basis of the memo filed by the petitioner's counsel that RC of the car was already transferred in favour of the first respondent.
The policy discloses that it was valid as on the date of accident.

As such, it can be said that the first respondent being the owner and second respondent being the insurer of the offending car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.4,02,000/- to the petitioner along with interest at 6% p.a., excluding Rs.30,000/- awarded towards future medical expenses, from the date of the petition till the deposit in Court.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.4 :

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3 as above and for the reasons stated therein , I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER

The claim petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 and 2, awarding compensation of Rs.4,02,000/- (Rupees four lakh two thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., excluding Rs.30,000/- awarded towards future medical expenses from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50% with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-0882 by its driver, dashed to the petitioner who was proceeding as pillion rider in the TVX XL motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-42-J-2187 and he sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 02.03.2021 ?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of rider of motor cycle ?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is he quantum of compensation and from whom?
4.
What order ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even by considering Exs.P.10 and P.11, it can be said that it is the driver of the car i.e., the first respondent who has caused the accident resulting in injuries to the petitioner.
Though the respondents have denied the accident and negligence aspect, but they have not chosen to place any cogent evidence to disprove the evidence placed by the petitioner.
Even the first respondent has not chosen to lead his evidence to controvert the evidence placed by the petitioner.
The conduct of the first respondent in not challenging the chargesheet itself is sufficient to draw an adverse inference against him that as the accident took place due to his negligence, he has remained silent.
As discussed above, this court has come to the conclusion that the evidence on record clearly establishes that sole negligence was on the part of the car driver and not the rider of the motorcycle.
Thus, by considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved that he met with an accident and sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M- 0882, whereas the first respondent has failed to prove that accident occurred on account of negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-42-J- 2187.
Merely because PW.2 is not the treated doctor of the petitioner, his evidence cannot be brushed aside when he is a competent person to assess the disability since he is also a senior consultant and DNB of Orthopaedics.
As the petitioner is an agriculturist, it can be said that the disability stated by PW.2 will definitely reduce the earning capacity of the petitioner to some extent.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
14. The learned counsel for the second respondent during his arguments, has submitted that as the rider of the motorcycle was riding it without having valid DL, due to his negligence also accident has occurred and as such, 25% of the contributory negligence has to be fixed on the rider of the motorcycle.
Nowhere in the written statement the second respondent has contended that the rider of the motorcycle has contributed negligence in occurring of the accident.
Therefore, the arguments of the learned counsel for the second respondent cannot be accepted.
opennyai_summary.decision:
16. In view of the reasons stated above, in all the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No.
a. Pain and Agony Rs. 50,000-00 b.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.4 :
In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3 as above and for the reasons stated therein , I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 and 2, awarding compensation of Rs.4,02,000/- (Rupees four lakh two thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., excluding Rs.30,000/- awarded towards future medical expenses from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50% with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
